questions.q: 2-Chloroethyl phenyl sulfide, C₆H₅S–CH₂CH₂–Cl, hydrolyses about 600 times faster than a comparable primary chloride. The intermediate responsible is:
questions.explain: The sulfur lone pair displaces chloride from the back to form a three-membered sulfonium ring, which water then opens quickly. A phenonium ion forms only when the aryl ring itself is on the β-carbon.

questions.q: A substitution that proceeds by neighbouring group participation at a stereocentre usually gives:
options: Inversion, because the external nucleophile attacks from the back
Retention, because two successive backside attacks occur
Inversion, because a free carbocation forms
questions.explain: The neighbouring group attacks with inversion, then the external nucleophile opens the ring with a second inversion; the two cancel to give retention.

questions.q: Under which condition is neighbouring group participation most likely to win over direct SN2 attack?
options: High concentration of a strong external nucleophile
Neighbouring group syn to the leaving group
No lone pair or π bond near the leaving group
Low concentration of a weak external nucleophile
questions.explain: The internal group is always present, so it wins when the outside nucleophile is scarce or weak. A concentrated strong nucleophile gives simple SN2 inversion, and the neighbouring group must be anti, not syn, to the leaving group.

questions.q: In a cyclohexane ring, a group Z with a lone pair sits on the carbon next to the carbon bearing the leaving group. Which statement is correct?
options: The trans isomer can show NGP and reacts faster; the cis isomer reacts by normal SN2 with inversion
The cis isomer shows NGP because Z and the leaving group are on the same face
Both isomers show NGP and react at the same rate
Neither isomer can show NGP because the ring is rigid
questions.explain: Z must reach the back of the C–Lg bond, which needs an anti arrangement, and only the trans isomer has it. The cis isomer cannot participate and gives ordinary SN2 inversion.
